text:
alice.chen: heads up, getting a big burst of SIEM alerts for api.key.use starting ~03:12 UTC, ~580 hits in 18m
ben.ortiz: I see it, lots of different src_ip but same service_account=obs-agent
carla: can you paste the query / sample logs so we can confirm UA and any error fields?
alice.chen: quick sample:
```
index=siem event=api.key.use service_account=obs-agent user_agent=\"obs-agent/2.1\" src_ip=* | stats count by src_ip
```
jamal.sre: that user agent is the telemetry agent we rolled last night, not surprising if there's a bug
siem-bot: Alert triggered: SIEM-RULE-API-KEY-ANOMALY (severity=medium) — 582 hits
carla: before we mute: check KMS unwrap/rotate activity and any kms:error entries in same window
alice.chen: checking KMS logs — unwraps are present but no failure codes, calls are originating from our internal KMS VPC range
ben.ortiz: also check recent infra changes — there was a canary update at 02:55 to the obs-agent that changed concurrency & retries
jamal.sre: if retries dropped backoff and increased fanout we can see many hits across ephemeral IPs (eg multiple pods)
carla: ok, this is likely a false positive due to the agent rollout. proposed short fixes: 1) add service_account allowlist for known telemetry agents, 2) change rule to use src_ip cardinality threshold, 3) add KMS-failure bypass to escalate only when unwrap errors > 0
alice.chen: suggested rule update: require (unique_ip_count > 8 AND hits_per_minute > 25) to fire for same svc_account; keep original thresholds for unknown svc_accounts
ben.ortiz: that sounds safe. we should also add a temporary suppression for obs-agent for 45m while infra patches the agent
carla: I'll draft the SIEM rule patch and suppression. also will spin up a dashboard widget to watch unique_ip_count per svc_account and a top-10 noisy rules panel
sie m-bot: (automated) rule SIEM-RULE-API-KEY-ANOMALY v1.1 queued for update by carla
carla: patch applied at 03:45 UTC: added svc_account allowlist, ip-cardinality gating, and KMS-error bypass. suppression: service_account:obs-agent duration:45m reason:\"telemetry rollout causing high fanout\"
jamal.sre: nice. let's add a runbook note under Security -> SIEM -> "API key high-volume" with steps to check deploys, KMS unwrap errors, svc_account UA, and apply suppression if correlated with a rollout
alice.chen: adding short checklist to runbook now. also filing an infra ticket to revert the retry change: TKT-7031
ben.ortiz: pinging infra-team: please prioritise a fix for the obs-agent retry/backoff regression, target rollback in next 30m
carla: sec-oncall-bot: created incident INC-2026-0321-02 — SIEM noise from obs-agent rollout, linked TKT-7031, assigned to infra-oncall
sec-oncall-bot: Incident created and notification sent to #incidents and infra oncall pager
alice.chen: once suppression expires we should run a check at 04:10 UTC and report whether alert volume normalized
jamal.sre: also schedule a 48h watch on that SIEM rule and alert if same svc_account generates >200 alerts/hr after suppression removed
carla: dashboard updated and pinned to eng-security. added panel: "SIEM noisy rules & top svc_accounts"
ben.ortiz: and add an automation to auto-suppress for known telemetry svc_accounts for short windows when deploys are ongoing (but with manual approval)
carla: noted — will add a policy doc for temporary suppressions tied to deploy tags
alice.chen: thanks folks. closing loop if no objections :thumbsup:
carla: summary: root cause = obs-agent rollout changed retry/backoff causing high-fanout api.key usage; remediation = temporary suppression + SIEM rule refinement (ip-cardinality + KMS-bypass) + infra ticket for revert; follow-up = dashboard + runbook entry + 48h monitoring
ben.ortiz: I'll take verification after infra deploys the revert and report back
jamal.sre: we'll remove suppression after alerts look normal for 2 consecutive checks
alice.chen: closing thread, will reopen if anything new appears
